findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() panics on any I/O failure
findings.failure_mode: untrusted or missing file path aborts the entire program instead of returning a typed error
findings.fix: return Result<Vec<Record>, std::io::Error> and propagate with ? or explicit Err

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() panics on non-numeric or missing field
findings.failure_mode: malformed CSV line causes panic instead of returning a typed parse error
findings.fix: return Result, use .parse().map_err(|e| ParseError(...)), and handle missing parts with .get(1).ok_or(...)

findings.problem: as u16 lossy cast truncates values above 65535 silently
findings.failure_mode: values in range 65536..=u32::MAX are silently truncated to u16 range, corrupting data
findings.fix: use u32::try_from(u32_value).map_err(...) or parse directly as u16 with parts[1].trim().parse::<u16>()

findings.problem: split(',').map(...).collect() then indexing parts[0] and parts[1] instead of split_once
findings.failure_mode: allocates a Vec of all parts unnecessarily, then risks index-out-of-bounds on malformed lines
findings.fix: use line.split_once(',').ok_or(MissingDelimiter) to get (name, rest) directly, then parse rest

findings.problem: parts[0] and parts[1] are unchecked indexed accesses on a Vec<String>
findings.failure_mode: a line with fewer than 2 comma-separated fields panics with index-out-of-bounds
findings.fix: use .get(0) and .get(1) with ok_or, or restructure with split_once as above

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) mixes I/O/logging into data parsing logic
findings.failure_mode: pure parsing is contaminated with side effects; parsing cannot be tested or composed without stdout interference
findings.fix: remove println! from the parsing pipeline; move logging to the shell layer after parsing completes

findings.problem: load_jobs returns Vec<Record> directly instead of Result, hiding all fallible operations
findings.failure_mode: all I/O, parse, and indexing failures are panics; callers cannot handle errors gracefully
findings.fix: signature should be pub fn load_jobs(path: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError>

findings.problem: parse::<u32>() then as u16 wastes allocation on wider type before truncation
findings.failure_mode: parse succeeds for values outside u16 range but silently truncates; also wastes the intermediate u32

findings.problem: no benchmark exists for load_jobs throughput or allocation behavior
findings.failure_mode: cannot verify if Vec allocation per line, collect(), or String::to_string() are acceptable for the workload
findings.fix: add criterion or custom benchmark measuring allocations, throughput, and memory for typical input sizes

findings.problem: no profiler evidence for hot-path allocation profile of load_jobs
findings.failure_mode: unknown if per-line Vec allocation + String allocation is the dominant cost; may over-optimize or under-optimize
findings.fix: run cargo-flamegraph or similar profiler on load_jobs with representative data

findings.problem: no second-ring evidence (allocations, command output) for the parsing path
findings.failure_mode: cannot prove whether split+collect+to_string is the right choice vs split_once+&str without measured data
findings.fix: add allocation tracking (e.g., alloc counter) or use cargo-bench with --output-json to capture allocation counts

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for load_jobs throughput or allocation behavior
no profiler evidence for hot-path allocation profile
no second-ring allocation or command evidence for parsing choices
